 Judgment
1. Both insurer as well as the claimant are in appeal challenging the following compensation awarded by the Tribunal:

Sl . Amount  Particulars  No. in (Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 10,40,052  2. Funeral expenses 15,000  3. Medical expenses and 15,000  transportation  4. Loss of love and affection 50,000  5. Loss of consortium to the 40,000  appellants  6. Loss of Estate 15,000  Total 11,75,052 2.

It is not in dispute that as a result of the motor vehicle accident which occurred on 11.08.2015,
Manjunath, a 46 years old died.
3. It is not in dispute that the Insurer is liable to pay the compensation as the offending vehicle was insured.
4. The insurer contends that the medical records indicates that the deceased was not wearing helmet and had consumed alcohol and therefore it would not be liable.
5. This argument is based on the emergency case record prepared by the NIMHANS.

Since there is no actual eyewitnesses for the accident and since the deceased was unconscious when he was brought to the NIMHANS, the entries made in the medical records cannot be conclusive regarding the non-wearing of helmet or there is also no records in the emergency case record Ex.R4 indicating that the deceased had consumed alcohol.

In that view of the matter, the argument that the insurer would not be liable for the compensation, cannot be accepted and the appeal of the insurer is Manager vs Smt. Gowramma on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1592800/
4 therefore dismissed.

sentences.text:
6. As far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, in order to arrive at the loss of dependency,
the Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.8,000/-.

As there is no credible evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2015, would be Rs.9,000/-.
7.
Since the deceased was aged 46 years and was self- employed, 25% is required to be added to the monthly income towards future prospects, which would result in the income to be Rs.11,250/-.
If 1/3rd is deducted towards personal expenses, his monthly income would be Rs.7,500/-.
8. The income of the deceased for the purposes of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.7,500/-.
9. As the deceased was aged 46 years, a multiplier of '13' would have to be applied.

Consequently,
the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.11,70,000/- (Rs.7,500 x 12 x 13 ) towards "loss of dependency".
10.

The claimants being the sons, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards "loss of consortium" i.e., in all Rs.88,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".
11. The sums as medical expenses of Rs.15,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and hence affirmed.

12. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 11,70,000  2. Loss of Consortium 88,000
3 . Conventional Heads 33,000
4. Medical expenses 15,000  Total 13,06,000 13.

Thus, the claimant would be entitled for compensation of Rs.13,06,000/- as against Manager vs Smt. Gowramma on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1592800/
5 Rs.11,75,052/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest from the date of petition till its realization.
14.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
15. The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum.
16. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
17. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal for disbursal in terms of the award.
18. The appeal of the claimants is accordingly allowed in part.
